name: Electronic and digital watch
region: Japan, the United States and Switzerland
summary: The watch with no hands and no spring. A quartz crystal keeps the time, and a red light or a grey liquid crystal shows the digits. The Seiko Astron of 1969 and the Pulsar of 1972 set it.

philosophy.core_thesis: A watch is an electronic instrument, so it shows the time as digits. A crystal with no moving parts keeps the time.
design_principles: Keep the time with a quartz crystal that vibrates 32,768 times each second.
Show the time as digits in red LED or in black on a grey LCD, with a seven segment shape for each digit.
Make the case in steel, gold or plastic, as a flat, bold shape with a square or a cushion form.
Hide the display until the user presses a button on the case side, for the early LED models.
Add functions in rows of buttons: date, alarm, stopwatch and a second time zone.
Make the case 30 to 45 mm wide and 8 to 12 mm thick, with a flat top and a clean face.
Use a black or a dark red display glass with no hands and no markers.
Price the watch by its function, so that a watch with more functions costs more.
anti_patterns: A hands dial with a printed quartz label
A case with engraved, chased or enamelled work
A display with a decorative font
A thick case with a heavy bezel
A face with markers that have no use
A leather strap with a fancy stitched edge

silhouette.shape: A flat case in a square, cushion or tonneau form. It has a blank black face and buttons on the side.
silhouette.line: Straight edges with rounded corners, a single plane on the top and a slim profile.
silhouette.fit: The watch lies flat on the wrist on a bracelet or a thin strap.
silhouette.proportion: Case thickness to width is about 1 to 4. The display fills about 50 per cent of the face. The digits are 6 to 8 mm tall.
rules: Use one display, one font and no dial print apart from small labels.
Place the buttons on the side, in a line, with the same size.
Make the case in one tone, so that the display provides the only contrast.
Keep the face free of marks except for brand and function labels.

fabrics.rule: Put the quartz crystal in a steel, plastic or gold case with a flat glass; show the time as red or grey digits.

methods: button on the side of the case
flat case with a snap-on or a screw-on back
construction.closures: A bracelet clasp or a pin buckle closes the strap; side buttons switch the display and the functions.
construction.details: A black glass face, digits in red or grey, a row of side buttons and a flat steel or plastic case.

surface.pattern: A black or red glass face with digits in a seven segment font and no other print.
surface.gloss: Brushed steel at 15 to 40 GU; the display glass at 80 to 95 GU; the plastic case at 40 to 70 GU.
surface.wear: The steel scratches, the plastic yellows, the display fades over decades and the rubber strap cracks.

palette.strategy: A dark face with one light colour for the digits; a steel, gold or black case.

processes: injection moulding of the plastic case
making.scale: From a few hundred gold watches in 1972 to millions of plastic watches a year in the late 1970s.
making.signs: No hands, digits in a seven segment shape, buttons on the side and a flat black face.

pieces.form: Flat steel case with a black face and red digits
Black plastic case with a grey liquid crystal display
Flat glass cover over the display
Gold case with a red display and a bracelet
Black rubber strap with a pin buckle

positive: red LED digits on black glass

emotion.target_response: A sense of the near future: the viewer sees a face without hands that shows the time in light.

use_cases: a prop for a film set in the 1970s or 1980s
an image prompt for a digital watch on a wrist
avoid_when: the brief wants a mechanical dial with hands
the brief wants a classic dress watch
the brief wants a hand made look

modifiers.how: Use a bright plastic case and strap, put a printed dial with hands in place of the display and add a pattern.
Use a colour screen that covers the face, add a digital crown and show apps in place of digits.
